{{Quote|A jungle world. Domed cities I see. Rodia it is.|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="CotF">{{TCW|Children of the Force}}</ref>}}
'''Rodia''', a [[Forest/Legends|rainforested]], industrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Tyrius system/Legends|Tyrius system]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]].

==Description==
{{Quote|I hope there's nothing out there that's particularly hungry.''"<br />"''I wouldn't count on that. But from what I know about Rodia, the locals have hunted all the big beasties to near extinction.|[[Shella Rinou]] and [[Kelric (Herglic)|Kelric]]|<ref name="ABVtR">{{WEGCite|story=A Brief Visit to Rodia|book=Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide}}</ref>}}
[[File:Rodia_palace.png|thumb|left|230px|Bubble-domed habitats on Rodia.]]
Rodia was a [[Temperature/Legends|hot]], [[Water/Legends|humid]] world which was covered in dense tropical [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]] which had been gradually giving place to sprawling [[City/Legends|cities]], [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] and industrial areas. Small axial tilt meant the climate was stable among the seasons. A large area of the planet was also covered in [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and there appeared to be two polar regions on the extreme latitudes. Landmasses were concentrated on two big continents—[[Betu/Legends|Betu]] in the western hemisphere, and [[Encheeko/Legends|Encheeko]] in the eastern—and several big islands between them. The empty [[Rodiak Ocean/Legends|Rodiak Ocean]] separated the two continents; the [[An'yettu Islands/Legends|An'yettu Islands]] spanned between the [[Ioliu Sea|Ioliu]] and the [[Wesessa Sea/Legends|Wesessa Seas]] among the continents.

The Rodians built their cities on waterways and protected them with environmental shields, [[Domed city/Legends|bubble domes]] that surrounded all habitation structures and allowed entry and exit for vehicles and vessels. These domes also protected from the extreme temperatures of the planet.<ref name="TCW-BJ" />

Two major cities on the planet were [[Equator City/Legends|Equator City]] and [[Iskaayuma/Legends|Iskaayuma]] which were the planetary capitals at different periods in Rodia's history. Equator City was the traditional capital until [[Navik/Legends|Navik]] usurped control over the planet and moved the capital to his clan's settlement at Iskaayuma.<ref name="SotEPG" />

Rodia's jungles used to host a variety of fauna and flora which were wiped out or made endangered over the millennia as the Rodians improved their technology and increased their population. Later cities sprawled over the reducing jungle areas.<ref name="SotEPG" /> 

The [[Rodian Karstag]], [[newoongall]] and the [[Ghest/Legends|ghest]] were native Rodian predators; however they were driven to near-[[extinction]] when the Rodians became the dominant species of the planet. They survived in smaller numbers in the deepest, isolated areas of the jungles. Some endangered specimens also were kept and bred by rangers, intended for the sport of wealthy Rodians.<ref name="SotEPG" />

Local animals, or the imported [[Cracian thumper]]s, were used as mounts by provincial Rodians, appropriate for the primitive roads in the remote countryside.<ref name="SotEPG" />

==History==
{{Quote|The history of Rodia explains much about how and why the Rodians think the way they do.|Excerpt from Obo Rin's ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy'', Revised Edition|<ref name="GG4">[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref>}}
===Early history===
Rodia was originally inhabited by rock-dwelling lizards which developed tools and weapons to aid in their survival.<ref name="TEGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> Over time, these evolved into the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Species/Legends|species]], who became brutal hunters to survive among the planet's dangerous wildlife. As they developed advanced technology, they began to exterminate the planet's other lifeforms at an increasingly rapid rate.<ref name="UAA" /> Eventually, all of the predators that threatened the Rodians were driven to extinction, and the Rodians began to hunt one another, finding or inventing excuses for war and laying waste to their homeworld's environment in the process.<ref name="TEGtAS" />

<div style="float:right">[[File:Rodian_War.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rodians often engaged in clan wars.]]</div>
As Rodian society developed and their technology improved, the leader of the most powerful clan, the [[Soammei clan]], eventually proclaimed himself ''Inta'si'rin'na'', or [[Grand Protector/Legends|Grand Protector]] of the Rodians. Through the rest of Rodian history, the title of Grand Protector shifted from clan to clan as loyalties and power shifted. Grand Protectors ruled all of Rodia as dictators.

===Discovery and Republic membership===
When [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] arrived on Rodia, the planet's ecosystem was on the verge of being damaged beyond repair.<ref name="UAA" /> The Rodians hunted the new arrivals down until their Grand Protector, recognizing the possibility of new prey to hunt off-world, called a halt to the violence.<ref name="GG4" /> A new policy was implemented; the Grand Protector declared that the best hunters, as proven by success in various gladiatorial contests and hunts on Rodia, would be allowed to leave the planet for work as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] or similar occupations. The Grand Protector's Hunters' Guild, or ''Goa-Ato'', instituted annual awards (or ''Atiang'') for the best hunters, with such categories as "Best Shot", "Longest Trail", or "Most Notorious Capture."

The Rodians eventually joined the Republic, fascinated by its [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and weapons.<ref name="UAA" /> Intergalactic trade boosted Rodia's technology by millennia.<ref name="SotEPG" /> By [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], Rodia was within [[Realspace/Legends|space]] that was considered well-explored,<ref name="TEA" /> and over time, the services of Rodian trackers became a popular export. Demand for weapons led to increased industrialization, especially around the megalopolis of Equator City. Rodian dramas also gained popularity;<ref name="TEA" /> [[Rodian Theater/Legends|Rodian Theater]] began as a simple series of staged fights, encouraged by Grand Protector [[Harido Kavila/Legends|Harido Kavila]] as a way for Rodians to burn off their aggression, but over time it developed into a vibrant, though violent, theatrical tradition. Though actors were barred from directly seeking political power at home, drama also became an acceptable way for dissident elements to challenge established ideas. Some Rodians illegally left their homeworld in search of refuge from clan feuds, traveling the galaxy freely and finding work in a variety of professions, from peaceful merchants and technicians to arms dealers and criminal henchmen. While the Rodian authorities treated off-world born Rodians as though they were alien galactic citizens, illegal emigrants were generally not allowed to return to Rodia, though some used forged or legitimate documents to claim off-world status.

[[File:Republicfrigate.png|thumb|left|230px|A [[Consular-class cruiser (Charger c70 retrofit)/Legends|Republic frigate]] over Rodia in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY.]]]]
During the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], an alliance of [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith]] and [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] won a [[Battle of the Tyrius system|battle]] at Rodia.<ref name="TEA" /> During the [[Mandalorian Wars]] Rodia remained neutral, but during the [[Jedi Civil War]] it was drawn into the full-scale conflict. [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] forces attempted to destroy the planet using the massive firepower of the [[Star Forge]] fleet, hoping to deny the Galactic Republic its greatest source of scouts and explorers. But the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] uncovered the plot and signaled the Republic fleet for help. The [[Battle of Rodia]] was an important battle of the Jedi Civil War, and after the Republic drove away the Sith fleet, Rodia officially joined the war on the Republic side, though individual Rodian mercenaries still worked for the Sith and other factions.<ref name="KotORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Following the [[Great Galactic War]], Rodia was annexed by the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] under the partial [[Treaty of Coruscant]]. This was received with much bitterness and outrage by the Rodian ambassador [[Mareesh]] who saw this as a betrayal by the Republic.<ref name="NGO">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order]]''</ref>

During the last days of the Republic, the planet was represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]], who was later appointed to the [[Loyalist Committee/Legends|Loyalist Committee]] as the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] worsened.<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|news/1359_4.html|Senator Farr Named to Loyalist Committee}}</ref> At some point during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], he betrayed his old friend Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] by luring her to Rodia and into the clutches of her old enemy, the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy/Legends|viceroy]], [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], in exchange for the shipment of supplies, which the Republic had failed to deliver, to his planet. He later realized his mistake and helped her escape.<ref name="TCW-BJ" /> Rodia thereafter remained loyal to the Republic, although it was near the front lines of combat and scarred by famine.<ref name="TEA" /> Rodia was never directly threatened by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], although negotiators were frequently sent by [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] to the city of Iskaayuma.<ref name="TCWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Later during the war, Farr bribed [[Ronet Coorr]] to divert naval forces from [[Iseno/Legends|Iseno]] to Rodia rather than to [[Duro/Legends|Duro]], resulting in Duro being taken by the Confederacy of Independent Systems in [[Operation Durge's Lance]]. Farr was forced to resign in disgrace.

===Imperial rule and Navik's coup===
<div style="float:right">[[File:Greedo-hd.png|thumb|left|180px|Greedo, a bounty hunter during the Imperial rule]]</div>
After the Clone Wars concluded in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Galactic Republic was reorganized into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Rodia and its population were spared enslavement under the new regime due to the Empire's demand for bounty hunters. In [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]], Rodia experienced an internal coup when Navik the Red of the [[Chattza clan/Legends|Chattza Clan]] conquered his rivals<ref name="TEA" /> in a series of fierce campaigns that spanned several [[Star system/Legends|star systems]]. After achieving victory, he named himself Grand Protector<ref name="SotES" /> and made his home city of Iskaayuma the new seat of government. Under Navik's rule, Rodia became a freer trading port and an emerging economic power.<ref name="TEA" /> Navik also tightened restrictions on emigration and built ties with [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] and the Galactic Empire. Navik ruthlessly persecuted his rivals, sentencing the entire [[Tetsu Clan]] to death. Even Tetsu refugees outside Rodia, such as [[Greedo the Elder]] and his family, were pursued by Chattza hunters. 

During the Imperial era, the urban areas of Rodia had expanded dramatically with their industrial districts expanding towards the once-dominating jungles; the expansion took no account or planning of the landscape and environment it occupied, resulting to congested, maze-like urban sprawls.<ref name="SotEPG" />

===Yuuzhan Vong conquest and beyond===
[[File:RodiaNEGAS.jpg|thumb|250px|Another view of Rodia]]
During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], [[Narik]] represented Rodia in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] until the planet was [[Battle of Rodia (Yuuzhan Vong War)|invaded and conquered]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] during their invasion of the galaxy.<ref name="Balance Point">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref>

During their invasion of the galaxy, the Yuuzhan Vong invaded Rodia to cut off the rimward portion of the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]]. As on many worlds, the Yuuzhan Vong conquerors began enslaving the population. The alien invaders planned to forge their Rodian captives into deadly warbeasts, under the direction of [[Master Shaper]] [[Taug Molou]]. He took his Rodian experimental subjects apart on a cellular level, reassembling their genetic code with bits from other creatures. This experiment resulted in the creation of the [[Vagh Rodiek]], mindless warbeasts that moved on crab-like legs with sharp half-meter long scythes of bone in place of arms. The Rodian natural head-spines were mutated into razor-sharp quills. Rodia itself was terraformed, with [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]-sized, leathery blossoms looming over the landscape.<ref name="TEA" />

The few Rodians who managed to flee Rodia found themselves refugees from persecution. Most however, hid in the jungle and launched guerrilla attacks against Yuuzhan Vong patrols. After that war, Rodia was represented in the [[Galactic Alliance Senate]] by [[Moog Ulur]]. Yuuzhan Vong terraforming made Rodia one of the most dangerous planets in the galaxy, filling its jungles with previously-unknown deadly predators. In a practice seen on [[Daluuj/Legends|Daluuj]]<ref name="Legacy 2">[[Legacy (2006) 2|''Legacy'' (2006) 2]]</ref> and other worlds, the Yuuzhan Vong also moved to Rodia, forming one of the largest known Yuuzhan Vong populations in the galaxy.<ref name="TEA" /> Over the next hundred years, the Rodians had reveled in the new dangers onworld and became even greater hunters than before. Under the Sith [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Empire]] led by [[Darth Krayt]], the planet claimed more Jedi bounties than any other, earning itself a favorable treatment from Darth Krayt.<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]'' claims Rodia has only two moons, but this was later corrected to four in their Errata and Official Clarifications.<ref name="Errata">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sagaederrata|text=Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Ed. Errata}}</ref>

Previously, Rodia was confirmed to a Mid Rim planet. In [[2008]], the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series changed the world from being a Mid Rim to an Outer Rim planet. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', released in [[2009]], also stated that Rodia was an Outer Rim planet.
